MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  May 12, 2020

Due to COVID-19 and the “Stay at Home” Order for the State of California and the Social
Distance Guidelines issued by Federal, State, and Local Authorities this Council Meeting was
conducted via Video Teleconferencing for all Council and Staff with the exception of the City
Attorney and City Clerk who were present in the Council Chamber. All public comments that
were emailed to the City Clerk were read during the meeting.

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Goodell
at 5:00 p.m., on May 12, 2020, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on May 7, 2020, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Teleconferenced:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Teleconferenced:  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services

Staff Present:  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel: Existing Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph 4 of
  Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 - Southwest Voter Registration Education Project
  v. The City of Mission Viejo

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Raised concerns with the City’s election system for November 2020
  and stated that the incumbents have a huge advantage because of the delay in adopting an
City Council Minutes  1  May 12, 2020
   election code with the election only 175 days away. She said voting is a right that belongs
  to the citizens and that the citizens are the ones to decide how its public officials are elected.

CS2. Liability Claims and Existing Litigation: Claimants: Donaldson, O’Brien, Peterson
  and Cunningham: Agency Claimed Against-City of Mission Viejo and: Significant
  Exposure to Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph (2) of Subdivision (d) of Section
  54956.9. (4 cases).

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there were two Closed Session items. The first was a
continued visitation of the Voting Rights Act matter and the second item was regarding present
litigation and torte claims. The City Council was updated on both matters but no reportable action
was taken.

INVOCATION: Council Member Sachs

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Goodell

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: Asked when City Council Meetings will be open to the public. He suggested
that the public could socially distance and wear masks in the Council Chamber.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Asked when the City Council Meetings will be open to the public. She gave
examples of surrounding cities that are holding public meetings and stated that it is unacceptable to
continue holding remote meetings.

DEPARTMENT HEAD UPDATES REGARDING COVID-19 ACTIVITIES

Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay

Public Services continues to provide essential services throughout the city. These include: pool
maintenance, landscape maintenance, street sweeping, trash collection, tree trimming for safety,
irrigation management and other services needed to ensure the facilities are kept safe, and that
potholes are repaired after the extensive rains of last week. Work is continuing on the construction
of Christopher Park and Craycraft Park. Both projects were held up with rain but they are slowly
working towards getting back on track with the installation of playground equipment at Christopher
Park. Grading and utility runs are being installed at Craycraft Park for the upgraded restroom
building. Staff also set up the drive through memorial display in the Kershaw Garden at the Civic
Center. Animal Services calls continue to be higher than normal and the officers are continuing to
address all calls that come into the shelter. Shelter staff are beginning to work on a re-opening plan
to include re-engaging the volunteers. Building services has implemented additional facility
cleaning and disinfecting operations at each of the City’s various sites. These cleanings focus on:
increased restroom deep cleaning to three times per day, upstaffed to have janitors focus on good,
sound cleaning and disinfecting of high-touched surfaces such as door handles, light switches, hand
rails, elevator buttons, sinks and faucets, restroom stalls and dispensers, vending machines and
counter tops, all tables and chairs used in our meeting rooms/banquet rooms are being disinfected
and tagged (NPM/Saddleback room), and added nightly cleaning to OCSD office at The Shops at
City Council Minutes  2  May 12, 2020
 Mission Viejo and all OCSD remote sites. The Building Services team worked with the Community
Relations department on preparing signs and producing sign holders for the reopening of the Tennis
Pavilion. The Golf Club reintroduced golf carts to the offering and they are being sanitized after
each use. The Club continues to have sold out weekend tee times and staff is beginning to work
with local vendors on a “Grab and Go” menu once food is being sold again at the golf course.

Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas

The department continues to be fully functional with no disruption to operations. To provide some
idea of the level of activity they have been experiencing since the stay at home order was issued,
the department has processed: 7 weekly check runs for a total of 584 checks worth approximately
$5.1 million; 976 individual refunds to customers for facility, class and program cancellations as
well as membership refunds due to COVID-19 worth a total of $116,000;306 individual deposits
to the City’s various bank accounts; 16 LAIF transfers to manage daily cash flow; 4 bi-weekly
payrolls; 33 unemployment claims; 41 new purchase orders and change orders; distribution of
almost 4,000 animal license renewal notices; and 7 billing invoices. Additionally, in the last 2
weeks, staff processed $3.6 million in budget adjustments approved at the last Council meeting due
to the effects of COVID-19. The focus has shifted to the 20/21 budget and after a comprehensive
review of City revenue, staff projects that General Fund revenue will be down approximately $3.6
million next year. Library Fund revenue is projected to decrease approximately $375,000. As was
the case when developing the 19/20 budget reduction plan, the goal is to cut appropriations in an
amount equal to the projected revenue reductions in order to maintain a balanced budget. Staff’s
review of the appropriation budget is on-going and they plan to bring an amended 20/21 budget to
Council on June 23, 2020.

Director of Community Development Elaine Lister

The Planning and Building counter, while not physically open to the public, is fully functioning and
operating. There are some inefficiencies in not having that direct public contact – certain things just
take longer - however, staff is very busy and plan checks and permits are reviewed and issued every
day. For the month of April: 152 Building Permits issued; 73 Plan Checks; 1,360 incoming calls;
and 3,188 emails received. Additionally, the Golf Course Vision Plan response was due last week
and the City received 10 proposals. Staff is also in full swing holding virtual web ex meetings.

Director of Information Technology Jackie Alexander

Information Technology continues to support City staff while they work remotely. Some staff return
to the office at different facilities as they open and those workers have a hybrid setup of working
from home and from the office. This poses additional security challenges that the IT department
continues to work on and address. As mentioned previously, although users are remote, their
helpdesk requests and needs remain at the same levels as previous levels because employees are
conducting all of their functions and job duties while working from home and because they have
full access to all the needed resources. IT department staff have been scheduling in-office work as
needed. The team, for the most part, is working remotely and keeping up the infrastructure and
security at the forefront of their duties. In addition to the Council meetings going virtual, there was
a successful Community Services Commission meeting held virtually and now others are queued
up to conduct theirs online. The Traffic Committee is scheduled for May 18 and the Investment
Advisory Commission is scheduled for May 20. IT staff built a dedicated web page just for virtual
commission meetings to help residents view the meetings live both on the website as well as on the
City Council Minutes  3  May 12, 2020
 City’s YouTube channel. The page also provides access to agendas and meeting documents to be
easily downloaded. Members of the public can submit comments on this page to engage and be part
of these virtual meetings. The URL is https://cityofmissionviejo.org/VirtualMeetings.

Director of Community Relations Karen Hamman

The Community Relations department was very pleased to obtain great media coverage as a result
of some of its recent press releases and proactive follow-up with the media. On Friday, NBC
reporter Vikki Vargas was in Mission Viejo to film spots on the reopening of the aquatics and tennis
facilities. The City also received some great coverage today from the Orange County Register on
the drive through American Heroes tribute - which is the only drive through display in Orange
County. The story will be in print tomorrow. The department continues a strong public outreach
campaign on social media channels, the website and through many emails and telephone calls daily.
Mission Viejo Television (MVTV) is still creating weekly videos with Mayor Goodell on a variety
of topics related to COVID-19. In last week’s episode MVTV visited the golf course a day before
it opened to take photos and videos of the newly-improved facility. This week’s message is about
the video tribute that the department is creating to celebrate Mission Viejo 2020 graduates. The
deadline for families to submit photos of their high school or college graduate is Sunday, May 17.
Community Relations staff have also been assisting the other departments with signage as they
begin plans for the reopening of City facilities and they are developing artwork for street banners
and emblems for several upcoming city-wide campaigns.

Director of Library Services Genesis Hansen

Library and Cultural Services staff continue to focus on wellness check calls. Since the last Council
meeting, they have called about 2,500 people, spoken with nearly 800, and helped 150 get
connected with resources. Staff have also been getting very positive feedback about the calls from
those they speak to and on social media. The Library’s Teen Advisory Board (TAB) has begun
writing letters to residents at Atria as a means of providing them with connection during a time of
isolation. They have an ongoing relationship with Atria and had a pre-COVID delivery service
there. The Director of Atria indicated that cards and letters to residents would be welcomed so the
TAB is working on writing them and they will be dropped off by staff in a safe manner. The Library
continues to check in items (2,300 since the last Council meeting) and to catalog and inventory
books while the Library is closed. On May 4, they hosted a live draw-along program on Instagram
with Disney artist Brian Kesinger. Even on short notice it was attended by nearly 80 people with
lots of engagement and participation. Staff have been working on phased reopening plans that are
context dependent so they can respond quickly to changes in guidance from the State, County, or
City. They are continuing to assist people in getting connected with online resources and checkouts
from the Overdrive downloadable books service has doubled over the same time period last year.

Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon

Construction activity continues to be high. SoCal Gas is performing about a half dozen different
pipeline/lateral replacement projects of aging infrastructure to improve safety. Likewise, Cox is
performing upgrades throughout the City in an effort to keep up with the increased internet demand
created by residents quarantined at home. In addition, Target, Amazon and Shea Homes all have
site improvements ongoing. Public Works is taking advantage of reduced traffic conditions to
perform long-needed replacement of underground traffic signal wiring conduit at two
intersections. Jeronimo/Acero was recently completed and Marguerite/Hillcrest is scheduled for
City Council Minutes  4  May 12, 2020
 next week. Public Works also hopes to take advantage of a favorable construction bid environment
to save money. While many agencies have put projects on hold, the City’s Residential Overlay
project went out to bid and the Arterial Highway Resurfacing project will be on the next Council
agenda for authority to advertise. With fewer projects bidding, staff is hopeful that will translate to
lower prices. Public Works also continues to pursue grant opportunities. On the agenda tonight is a
request to apply for an OCTA grant which will provide 80% funding for a $200,000 project to
install about 60 catch basin debris screens throughout the Civic Core area. These screens will help
keep trash and other debris out of the natural waterways. Staff is also pursuing a “Go Human” mini-
grant recently brought to their attention by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley. This program encourages
agencies to partner with community organizations in support of bike and pedestrian safety so staff
is working with both school districts to apply for crosswalk improvements at schools throughout
the City.

Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix

Last Friday, the City opened the Marguerite Tennis Pavilion which is now open 6 days a week for
morning and evening play. Over the four days since opening, social distancing requirements have
been managed and staff have been keeping the facility clean. 166 people have played with an
additional 27 private one-on-one lessons being offered. Nurses Day was May 6, 2020, and with the
help of Mayor Goodell, staff was able to mail thank-you letters to the nurses who usually volunteer
at the Murray Center when it is open. They check blood pressure and administer flu shots for the
patrons. Staff have also been working with many organizations within the community to accept
donations such as quilts/blankets, masks, gift cards, etc. to give to homebound seniors and other
organizations in need. The City has been in contact with over 150 senior living establishments
throughout Mission Viejo to check on them and see if they have any needs. Most of them have
indicated they need help securing basic PPE items such as masks and sanitizer. Based on these
needs, the City was able to place orders for supplies and staff we have begun distributing these
items to the senior facilities. We have distributed over 400 masks, gloves and sanitizers with more
distributions set for this Friday. Food and nutrition programs continue to be popular: every other
week a mix of staff and volunteers are packaging and delivering perishable food items to seniors
living at the Heritage Villas. The City is working with Jamboree Housing to secure volunteers to
help harvest food at OCC and distribute the produce to seniors in need. Over the past two weeks
staff have worked with Agewell Senior Services to deliver over 3,200 meals through the home
delivered meals program. Weekly Park-It Market programs continue and more and more are taking
advantage of all of these resources. The Hygiene Donation Program collected another $7,000 worth
of donated goods and the two groups benefitting from this program are Stand Up for Kids and OC
Rescue Mission. There are still collection bins for hygiene items located at City Hall and the Murray
Center. Staff also hosted a food drive on May 2 at the Murray Center and the community exceeded
expectations with over 8,000 pounds of food that was then bagged and distributed to those in need
in Mission Viejo. The leftovers were then donated to South County Outreach to help others
throughout the County. The next food drive at the Murray Center will be held on Saturday, May 16
between 9 and 11 a.m. Staff have conducted approximately 1,500 wellness check phone calls and
people are appreciative and many say they look forward to these calls each week. One of the biggest
benefits is relaying resources to seniors within the community regarding food, senior hours at
grocery stores, transportation, etc. Staff also worked with Mission Viejo Christian Church and
through the efforts of the Community Relations and IT Departments, the City was able to invite the
community to an online National Night of Prayer program. Staff continues preparing for a virtual
Memorial Day Ceremony which will be played on Memorial Day throughout the day on the City’s
YouTube channel and MVTV.

11. Local Emergency For COVID-19 Update

  Emergency Operations Manager Paul Catsimanes updated the City Council with current
  information including the following.

  As of today there are 3,602 positive cases of COVID-19 in Orange County with cumulative
  deaths at 77. Statewide positive cases total 69,382 with deaths reaching 2,847. Nationally
  there are 1.3 million positive cases with 80,820 deaths. Executive Management continues to
  meet in the City’s Emergency Operations Center (EOC) via teleconferencing 3-4 days per
  week. The Orange County Operational Area EOC holds a teleconference call for local
  jurisdictions every Thursday led by Orange County Health Care Agency which provides the
  latest statistics and guidance related to the spread of COVID-19. Information shared as part
  of this call includes cumulative positive tests, fatalities, testing counts, hospital bed counts,
  and bed capacity. Over the past ten days hospital bed capacity has been running lower than
  average ranging from 54% to 58%. Mission Hospital is reporting that they are scheduling
  previously deferred elective and non-essential procedures as the capacity has maintained a
  manageable level. Space is still open for potential surge in COVID-19 patients and across
  Orange County many hospitals have increased surge capacity by setting up field treatment
  tents on hospital grounds. As of today, there are 230 individuals hospitalized with COVID-
  19 with 100 of these patients in ICU. Orange County Healthcare reports that COVID-19
  testing continues to be focused on the seriously ill, medical response personnel, and/or other
  essential personnel who are exhibiting symptoms. Members of the public at large who are ill
  and exhibit symptoms which may include a high fever, sore throat, and difficulty breathing
  are encouraged to call their medical provider to seek treatments and inquire about testing
  options based on their individual circumstances. Currently, there are 13 public health Orange
  County COVID-19 testing network sites throughout Orange County. These testing network
  sites are safety net locations offering testing to symptomatic individuals that include a
  medical assessment. These sites are being promoted for testing of specific asymptomatic
  health care workers and others working in congregant living settings. Additional information
  can be found at http://occovid19.ochealthinfo.com/covid-19-testing-and-screening. With
  respect to the expansion of testing, the Orange County Health Care Agency reported that it
  is their goal to increase testing from the current average daily test count of approximately
  1,000 tests per day to 4,000 test per day over the next month. This will be accomplished by

City Council Minutes  7  May 12, 2020
   increasing the number of testing locations. Over the past week State and County testing
  locations increased from 9 to 13 locations. Over the next month Orange County Health Care
  Agency’s goal is to move toward asymptomatic testing based on state guidance and serology
  testing which is the antibody testing. Currently residents can go to LabCorp and Quest Lab
  for antibody testing. Orange County Health Care Agency reported that the biggest hurdle to
  testing expansion is the depleted levels of the extraction kits used for the antigen testing and
  efforts are underway to augment current levels of testing supplies. This past week a State
  Test Center opened in Mission Viejo at Share Ourselves Clinic located at 27725 Santa
  Margarita Parkway. Symptomatic individuals are able to call and speak to a physician over
  the phone to be evaluated and scheduled for an appointment. Related to Personal Protection
  Equipment (PPE), City staff is ordering items such as additional masks, gloves, and hand
  sanitizer for employees which are seemingly more readily available now. This is in order to
  be prepared for the eventual re-opening of City facilities. Finally, the City reinstituted blood
  drives at City facilities as part of the maintenance of essential medical services in the County.
  Today, the City of Hope conducted a blood drive which is just now concluding and there
  were more than 50 donors register. Based on the latest numbers, there were approximately
  44 units collected. Two future American Red Cross Blood Drives are being scheduled at the
  City for the month of June and the City will be messaging out to the community the exact
  dates and times once they are confirmed. In all the blood drives, distancing and disinfection
  of surfaces is conducted for the safety of donors and blood drive staff. A special thanks to
  the City of Hope and the community for showing up for the donations.

17. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

City Council Minutes  9  May 12, 2020
   By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum shared that although she is not physically attending meetings, she is
participating in a variety of virtual meetings. This past week she attended Sheriff Barnes’
presentation on Orange County community updates and she thanked Saddleback Church for hosting
that meeting. She also participated in the Southern California Association of Government (SCAG)
meeting virtually and stated that it was a lot easier than driving to Los Angeles. Council Member
Bucknum further outlined her attendance in the Association of California Cities virtual installation
conducted by Senator Moorlach; the National Day of Prayer hosted virtually by the Mission Viejo
Christian Church; and the virtual Rotary Club breakfast.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths thanked the Mayor for everything he is doing. He also announced that he is
getting a lot of feedback from residents on re-opening of businesses in Mission Viejo. He thanked
the Rotary Club for cleaning up weeds at the Mission Viejo Post Office this past Sunday and
outlined his virtual attendance in the Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG)
Environment and Energy meeting. He said there was nothing to report other than the fact that it was
much easier to participate in a Zoom meeting than to drive to Los Angeles. Council Member Raths
noted that people are getting antsy to get out and he asked residents to be patient. He reminded the
community that the City does not own the Lake, but rather it is a private association. In closing,
Council Member Raths announced that he joined a personal lawsuit with Council Members from
Dana Point and San Clemente which has nothing to do with the City but is concerning the opening
of the beaches in Orange County.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs joked that at this point, after all this time in sequestration, he and his wife
are still extraordinarily happily married and able to live with one another in the same room. He
stated that the idea of getting the City and its businesses back open is extraordinary and he has never
seen anything like this in his lifetime. He expressed concern for the lack of leadership in the
communities and said he feels there is no aggressive leadership from the County and certainly not
from the Senate, Assembly and Governors office. Council Member Sachs said what is going on
right now is a trampling on the Bill of Rights and the Declaration of Independence. He noted that
he listened to a recent symposium and one of the participants tried to determine how many of the
80,000+ unfortunate deaths listed as COVID-19 on the Center for Disease Control’s website were
being attributed to the flu and other pneumonia type deaths. This person was unable to find the data.
Council Member Sachs said he is not taking this lightly but feels that it is time to move on and open
the City. He posted, on his personal Facebook page, the question “Should Mission Viejo consider
opening businesses in the City as all businesses are essential?” and overwhelmingly, not one person
objected to opening the City and businesses. Council Member Sachs said that people are given the
choice of free will and are able to make decisions for themselves. Lastly, he stated that he yearns
for leadership from the State.

City Council Minutes  10  May 12, 2020
 Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that she too is attending a lot of virtual meetings. One of the fun
events was the National Day of Prayer with Mission Viejo Christian Church via Facebook and she
thanked Pastor Mike for hosting. She reminded residents that all churches are conducting online
services and her church has a daily devotional and bible study so she encouraged residents to seek
out these opportunities. Along with Community Services Manager Drew Fine, Mayor Pro Tem
Kelly said she participated in a Zoom Meeting hosted by Saddleback Church regarding their
outreach team. The Church will be conducting pop-up pantries and they will start with the Casta
del Sol and Heritage Villas senior communities. They have offered to provide a job fair once the
City is open and Saddleback Church will also be hosting a three-day Blood Drive in their worship
center, May 19-21 from 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. each day. In addition to this, the City will be holding
a Blood Drive on June 11 (sponsored by Senator Pat Bates) and another one on June 22. Both will
be held in the Saddleback Room at City Hall. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley said these drives are an
essential service as there is a demand for blood at this time so she encouraged residents to go online
and sign-up. She also announced that she participated in the South Orange County Coalition’s 2020
Economic Report given by Dr. Christopher Thornberg. She said the information is available on
their website and Dr. Thornberg feels the economy will be back on track by the end of the year.
Mayor Pro Tem Kelley commended Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon for going after grants
for school safety through the Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG). She also
commended City Manager Wilberg and staff for all their hard work during this time. Lastly, Mayor
Pro Tem Kelley encouraged everyone to shop Mission Viejo and continue to stay strong.

Mayor Goodell

Mayor Goodell announced that he donated blood at Mission Viejo Christian Church about a month
ago and he indicated that there are many blood donation centers if residents can’t make the dates
that Mayor Pro Tem Kelley outlined. He thanked everyone that is guiding the City through this
crisis. He said the City’s leadership are not trying to keeps things closed but are trying to follow the
State Constitution and the Constitution of the United States of America, which state that there are
certain things that must be followed in order to be in compliance with the law. Mayor Goodell said
that in order to meet all the needs of the community at-large and each resident, the City wants
everyone to be safe and healthy and get through this crisis stronger than ever. He announced that
he is attending weekly meetings with all the Mayors of Orange County on Thursday nights and on
Fridays, he meets with the Orange County CEO, Chairman of the Board of Supervisors, and the
County Health Officer to discuss how to get cities and the County open. Mayor Goodell noted that
he has also joined on several letters to Congress and to the President for the next round of stimulus
money to fund cities and counties directly. The County received some of the first monies to backfill
all the COVID-19 testing but it did not fund cities under 500,000 in population, which is every city
in Orange County. He said that cities are asking for that support to help backfill lost revenues from
property taxes, sales taxes and fees they are missing. In closing, Mayor Goodell expressed his
appreciation for everything City staff, consultants and elected leaders are doing and said he looks
forward to the light at the end of the tunnel.

ADJOURNMENT
